newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee exports drop in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee exports drop in latest week.

text.p: There was a major drop in registrations for coffee for export in Uganda this week, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Friday.
It said total coffee registrations amounted to 24,380 60-kg bags compared to 348,046 bags in the previous week.

The standard Robusta Screen 15 grade still dominated the market, contributing 21,321 bags. Last week, its contribution amounted to 145,502 bags. Screen 12 and Screen 18 contributed 1,046 bags and 1,080 bags respectively compared to 52,612 bags and 41,497 bags in the previous week.
Arabica drugar accounted for 300 bags, down from 10,000 bags in the preceeding week. Grade 1199 accounted for 333 bags while the remainder was supplied by other grades.

Local prices ranged between 1,250 and 1,300 Ugandan shillings compared to 1,150 to 1,250 in the previous week for a kg of fair average quality (FAQ) coffee. Kiboko prices ranged between 600 and 650 shillings from 500 last week.
Arabica parchment oscillated between 1,400 and 1,500 shillings from 1,350 to 1,450 previously.

The highest price recorded for Robusta Screen 15 was 69 cents per lb compared to 63.71 cents last week. The lowest price for the same grade was 58.70 cents per lb from 58 cents last week, according to UCDA figures.
The price for drugar arabicas was 104 cents per lb compared to 110 per lb in the preceeding week.
UCDA expected prices in the international market to remain steady.
